And he the rather brings this Instance, lest the <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi> should Accuse him of Inso<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lency; for that he had spoken before only of himself: and therefore he gives them to understand, that there were many other believing <ns0:hi>Israelites,</ns0:hi> as well as him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self; though possibly they were unknown to them. You know (saith he) what the Scripture saith of <ns0:hi>Elias,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 19.</ns0:note>? how he <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>bringeth a charge.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLunhyphen" />keth intercession to God against Israel <ns0:hi>t,</ns0:hi> saying.<ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Against the <ns0:hi>Ten Tribes,</ns0:hi> who were generally Revolted from God, and fallen to <ns0:hi>Idolatry</ns0:hi>: Against those he complained, or those he impeached, ripping up their Impieties, as in the folowing words.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3. Lord, they have killed thy prophets <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Vid.</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 19.10, 14.</ns0:note>, and digged down thine altars <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">These were not the <ns0:hi>Al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tars</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>high-places,</ns0:hi> for they are Commended that cast them down; nor the <ns0:hi>Altars</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Temple</ns0:hi> at <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> for they were out of the reach of the <ns0:hi>Ten Tribes,</ns0:hi> against whom <ns0:hi>Elias</ns0:hi> complains: But such <ns0:hi>Altars</ns0:hi> (say some) as the Godly of the <ns0:hi>Ten Tribes,</ns0:hi> did Build to serve God with, when they were not permitted to go up to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi>; in which Case, the Building of private <ns0:hi>Altars</ns0:hi> (as some learned <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> have affirmed) was allowed. Or else by <ns0:hi>Altars,</ns0:hi> you may understand such <ns0:hi>Altars,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Elias</ns0:hi> himself, by the special Commandment of God, had <ns0:hi>Erected.</ns0:hi> Others, by <ns0:hi>digging down</ns0:hi> God's <ns0:hi>Altars,</ns0:hi> do understand their Corrup<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ting, and Destroying the <ns0:hi>true Worship of God</ns0:hi>; and the Words are to be taken Synecdoctically, or Metonimically; the Sign being put for the Thing signified.</ns0:note>, and I am left alone <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">So it was for ought he knew; for few, if any did publickly own the <ns0:hi>true worship of God:</ns0:hi> So generally was the Defection of the <ns0:hi>Ten Tribes</ns0:hi> in those Dayes.</ns0:note>, and they seek my <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>my soul.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> life.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4. But what saith the answer of God <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">The word properly signifieth the <ns0:hi>Oracle,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Answer of God</ns0:hi> given in the <ns0:hi>Tabernacle</ns0:hi> from the <ns0:hi>Mercy-Seat</ns0:hi>; but it is generally taken for any divine Answer or Direction received from God, <ns0:hi>vid. Mat.</ns0:hi> 2.12. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 11.7. where the same Word is used. The Apostle doth not repeat the whole <ns0:hi>answer of God,</ns0:hi> as it is Recorded in 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 19.15, 16, 17, 18. but so much only as was pertinent to his pur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pose.</ns0:note> unto him? I have reserved to my self <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">He saith not, they have reserved themselves, but <ns0:hi>I have reserved</ns0:hi> them. <ns0:hi>q. d. Of my own Free-grace I have kept them from Idolatry and Apostacy.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> seven thou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sand men <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">A certain Num<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ber for an uncertain. There were doubtless Women amongst them; but they are noted by the more worthy Sex.</ns0:note>, who have not bowed the knee to <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>to <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">

                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>the image of</ns0:hi> Baal <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">The word <ns0:hi>Image,</ns0:hi> is not in the <ns0:hi>greek</ns0:hi>; but the Article being of the <ns0:hi>Feminine gender,</ns0:hi> it was necessarily un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstood.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5. <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> Even so then at this present time al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />so, <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>there <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> been.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> there is a remnant according to the electi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of grace <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> As it was in the times of <ns0:hi>Elias,</ns0:hi> so it is now; <ns0:hi>there is a remnant</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> which God hath graciously <ns0:hi>elected</ns0:hi>; therefore their <ns0:hi>rejection</ns0:hi> is not Total, which was the thing to be proved. Though those that Believe are <ns0:hi>few,</ns0:hi> in respect of the those that Believe not; as <ns0:hi>a remnant</ns0:hi> is but little, in respect of the whole Piece; yet there are many Thousands of them, as <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> said to <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> Act. 21. 20. <ns0:hi>Thou seest Brother, how many thousand Iews there are which believe.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:425" />6. And <ns0:note place="margin">See Deu. 9.4.</ns0:note> if by grace, then <ns0:hi>is it</ns0:hi> no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if <ns0:hi>it be</ns0:hi> of works, then it is no more grace: o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />therwise work is no more work <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">This Verse depends upon the former; and though it doth not seem to appertain to the Argument the Apostle had in hand, yet, by the Direction of the Spirit, he takes the little Occasion that is offered, to shew, That <ns0:hi>election</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>vocation</ns0:hi> is only by <ns0:hi>grace,</ns0:hi> and not by <ns0:hi>works</ns0:hi>; this he had spoken to before, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 4.4, 5. and 9.11. But he toucheth upon it again; and here he delivers a Truth, which the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> of Old, either could not, or would not understand, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> That there is no mixing of the Merit of <ns0:hi>good works,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>free-grace</ns0:hi> of God; but one of these doth exclude and destroy the Nature of the other: For if <ns0:hi>election</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>calling</ns0:hi> were both of <ns0:hi>grace</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>works</ns0:hi> (as some that call themselves Christians, as well as the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> af<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />firm) then <ns0:hi>grace is no grace,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>works are no works:</ns0:hi> For whatsoever proceedeth of <ns0:hi>grace,</ns0:hi> that cometh Freely, and not of Debt; but what cometh by Merit of <ns0:hi>works,</ns0:hi> that cometh by Debt; but now Debt and no Debt, or that which is Free, and by Desert, are quite contrary things. Therefore to say, That Men <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>re <ns0:hi>elected</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>called,</ns0:hi> partly of <ns0:hi>grace,</ns0:hi> and partly of the Merit of fore-seen <ns0:hi>works,</ns0:hi> that were to put things together, that cannot Agree, to make Debt no Debt, Merit no Merit, <ns0:hi>works no works, grace no grace</ns0:hi>; and so to Affirm and Deny one and the same thing.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7. What then <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> My Discourse comes to this, or this is the Sum of it.</ns0:note>? Israel hath not obtained that which he seeketh for <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> The Body of the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Nation, seeking <ns0:hi>righteousness</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>life</ns0:hi> by the <ns0:hi>works of the law,</ns0:hi> have not ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tained it, or they have not hit the Mark; they Aimed at it, but they Shot wide; they took a great deal of Pains, to little or no purpose, <ns0:hi>vid. chap.</ns0:hi> 9.31.</ns0:note>; but the election <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> The Elect; the Abstract for the Concrete; so before, Circum<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cision for the Circumcised.</ns0:note> hath obtained it, and the rest were <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 paragraph">
                        <ns0:desc>〈1 paragraph〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> blin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ded <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Those who are not Elected; they are left by God's just Judgment to their own Ignorance and Obdurateness: As also to Satan, who doth increase it in them, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 4.4. The Antithesis re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quires, that he should have said, <ns0:hi>The rest have not obtained</ns0:hi>; but he speaks this of purpose, to shew the Cause of their not Obtaining, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Their own <ns0:hi>blindness of mind,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>hard<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness of heart.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8. According as it is written <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Viz</ns0:hi> In <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 6.9. and 29.10.</ns0:note>, God hath given them the spirit <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 paragraph">
                        <ns0:desc>〈1 paragraph〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> of slumber <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">The word signi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fieth, such a <ns0:hi>dead sleep,</ns0:hi> as those have, who are pri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t or stung with venemous Beasts, out of which, they hardly or never Awake.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 12.2. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 13.14.</ns0:note> eyes that they should not see, and ears that they should not hear, unto this day <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> So it was of old, and so it is still. Or else these words (the former being included in a Pa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />renthesis) may be joyned with the last words of the foregoing Verse; thus the Rest are <ns0:hi>blinded unto this day.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9. And David saith <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Viz.</ns0:hi> In <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 69.22, 23. The Apostle tyeth not him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self to the very words of the <ns0:hi>Psalmist,</ns0:hi> but being guided by the same Spirit, by which <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> Wrote, he adds and alters some words, without diminishing the Sence.</ns0:note>, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumbling-block, and a recompence unto them <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Some take these words for a Prayer. Others a Prophesy. <ns0:hi>Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid</ns0:hi> in the Person of <ns0:hi>Christ</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> (of whom he was a Type) doth Complain and Prophesy of the extream Injuries and Oppressions, wherewith the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> (his own People) should Vex Him; as that they should give Him <ns0:hi>gall for meat,</ns0:hi> and in his <ns0:hi>Thirst,</ns0:hi> give Him <ns0:hi>vinegar to drink, ver.</ns0:hi> 21. There<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore by way of Imprecation, he Prayeth down the <ns0:hi>wrath of God</ns0:hi> upon them<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Particularly he Prophesies or Prays, That all their most Pleasant Things might be turned to their Destruction; that their Understandings might be Darkned, so as they shall discern nothing of Heavenly Things; that they might savour nothing but earthly things, and be unable to lift up Heads and Hearts to God, and to his Gospel. Now <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> having, by a Spirit of Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phesy, prayed down such Miseries upon the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> they must be Fulfilled; therefore the general <ns0:hi>unbelief,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>hardness of heart,</ns0:hi> that is amongst that People, is not to be wondered at.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 Let their eyes be darkned, that they may not see, and bow down their back al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />way.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 I say then <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Hitherto he hath shewed, that the rejection of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> is not <ns0:hi>totall.</ns0:hi> Now he comes to prove that it is not <ns0:hi>final</ns0:hi>; that before the end of the World, they shall be generally called and converted, that they together with the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> that believe, <ns0:hi>shall make one Sheepfold, and one Flock under one Shepherd the Lord Iesus Christ.</ns0:hi> And for the proving of this, diverse Arguments are brought by the Apostle (who alone plainly handles this secret) on which he insisteth the longer for the com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fort of the Poor <ns0:hi>Iewes,</ns0:hi> as also for the Administration and Information of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, Have they stumbled, that they should fall? God forbid <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Here is another Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lepsis or Anticipation. The <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi> might say, if the case be thus, that these Holy Prophets <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> have foretold our <ns0:hi>Blindness and Stumbling,</ns0:hi> then we are in a hopeless condition, and that for ever. To this he an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swers, That they have not so stumbled, as that they should finally <ns0:hi>fall,</ns0:hi> so as never to rise again; Far be it from me to affirm any such things: God hath revealed the contrary to me: that he will one day call the <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi> again, and restore them to his favour.</ns0:note>: but <ns0:hi>rather</ns0:hi> through their fall salvation <ns0:hi>is come.</ns0:hi> unto the Gentiles <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> Out of the forementioned Evil, there ariseth this good, that the Gospel (being rejected by the <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi>) is Preached to the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> and they are thereby called and brought to Sal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vation, <ns0:hi>vid. Act.</ns0:hi> 13.42, 46. Because now at first a few <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi> only, and a multitude of <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> are converted, it hath so fallen out, that the Ceremonial Law is the more easily abrogated, and the Doctrine of the Gospel, and the Grace of God is the better established.</ns0:note>, for to provoke them to jeaalou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sie <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi> who embrace not the Gospel. <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> This Grace that God hath bestowed upon the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> he will make use of in his appointed time, as a prick of holy Jealousy to the <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi>; he will by means thereof, stir them up to a holy Indignation and Emulation, to see themselves so far outstript by those whom they Contem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ned, and thereupon to Embrace the Gospel, and become the People of God again. Thus as God hath ordered, <ns0:hi>That the casting away of the Iewes, should be an occasi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of the Calling of the Gentiles:</ns0:hi> so again on the other hand, the Calling of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> shall be an occasion of the restoring of the <ns0:hi>Iewes.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12. Now if the fall of them <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> the riches of the world, and the <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>the pa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                        <ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />city of them.</ns0:hi> Or, <ns0:hi>the decay,</ns0:hi> or, <ns0:hi>loss.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> diminishing of them the riches of the Gentiles <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Another Anticipation. The Apostle having shewed, <ns0:hi>That the falling away of the Iewes,</ns0:hi> was an occasion <ns0:hi>of the comming in of the Gentiles,</ns0:hi> it might be Objected, That the <ns0:hi>Conversion</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>the Iewes</ns0:hi> might likewise be an occasi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>f the falling away of the Gentiles.</ns0:hi> To this he An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swers Negatively, and confirmes his Answer by an Ar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gument from the less to the greater; that if their Fall and Diminution were the riches of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> their Calling again would be so much more, <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> if God hath made use of the <ns0:hi>Fall</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Rejection</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Iewes,</ns0:hi> for an occasion of powring out the riches or abundance of his grace upon the Nations, and of the number of believ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing <ns0:hi>Iewes,</ns0:hi> being so very small (which is meant by their diminishing) hath occasioned the <ns0:hi>Conversion</ns0:hi> of such a multitude of <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> Then how much more will their fullness have the Effect?</ns0:note>: how much more their fullness <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Their general Conversi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on, the comming in of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> shall so fill the World with Wonder, and the Gospel with Lustre, that a much farther Accession will be made even to the num<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ber of the believing <ns0:hi>Gentiles.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13. For I speak to you Gentiles, in as much as I am the apostle of the Gentiles, I magni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fy mine office <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> I speak to you of being Rich in the Faith a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bove the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> because I challenge a special interest in you, <ns0:hi>in as much as I am appointed to be the Apostle of the Gentiles,</ns0:hi> and am sent chiefly unto them, <ns0:hi>vid. chap.</ns0:hi> 15.16. <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 9.15. and 13.2. and 22.21. and 26.17. <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 1.16. and 2.7. <ns0:hi>Ep<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>s.</ns0:hi> 3.8. 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.11. And therefore in thus setting forth your Priviledges and Blessings, <ns0:hi>I mag<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nify mine Office.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14. If by any meanes I may provoke to emulation <ns0:hi>them which are</ns0:hi> my flesh, and might save some of them <ns0:hi>g.</ns0:hi>
                  <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> And I thus Extol Gods Favour and Mercy to you, that it may be a meanes (if God please) to provoke the <ns0:hi>Iews, that are my own flesh and blood,</ns0:hi> to a holy <ns0:hi>Emu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lation</ns0:hi> o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>jealousy, (vid. v.</ns0:hi> 11.) when they shall see the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> possess what was promised to them. <ns0:hi>Q.</ns0:hi> How doth he say, That he may save some of them! is not God the Author of Salvation? <ns0:hi>A.</ns0:hi> Yes: but he hath given his Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nisters to be Instruments therein, and called them <ns0:hi>Fel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />low workers with himself,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 6.1. <ns0:hi>vid.</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 4.16.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:426" />15. <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">This verse containes an Argument to prove the <ns0:hi>Cal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ling of the Iewes</ns0:hi>; not a new one, but that repeated which you had before <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 12. the substance is the same, only the terms differ: there he spake of the Fall and di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />minishing of the <ns0:hi>Iewes,</ns0:hi> here, of their casting away; there it was the riches, here it is the reconciling of the World. <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> If the rejection of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> brought great pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fit to the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> their Reception and Restauration will bring abundantly more.</ns0:note> For if the casting away of them <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> the reconciling of the world <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> An occasion of Preach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the Gospel to the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> by meanes of which, they were <ns0:hi>reconciled to God.</ns0:hi> The Gospel is the Ministery of Reconciliation, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 5.18, 19<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 20.</ns0:note>; what <ns0:hi>shall</ns0:hi> the receiving <ns0:hi>of them be</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">into the favour of God and the bosome of the Church.</ns0:note>, but life from the dead <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">A proverbial Speech, to signify a great Change for the better. The Conversion of that People and Nation will strengthen the things that are languishing, and like to dye in the Christian Church. It will confirm the Faith of the <ns0:hi>Gen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiles,</ns0:hi> and Reconcile all their Differences in Religion, and occasion a more thorow Reformation amongst them: there will be a much more happy and flourishing Estate of the Church, even such as shall be in the end of the World, at the <ns0:hi>Resurrection of the Dead.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16. <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>and if.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> For <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Here is another Argument to prove the <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi> are not finally <ns0:hi>Rejected,</ns0:hi> because of the Covenant made with their Fathers.</ns0:note> if the first-fruit <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Some make a difference between the <ns0:hi>the first-Fruit,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Root,</ns0:hi> in the latter part of the verse. By <ns0:hi>the first-Fruit,</ns0:hi> they understand the <ns0:hi>Apostles,</ns0:hi> and other godly <ns0:hi>Iewes,</ns0:hi> that were at first Converted to the <ns0:hi>Christian Faith</ns0:hi>; and by the <ns0:hi>Root,</ns0:hi> they understand <ns0:hi>Abra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ham</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Patriarchs.</ns0:hi> Others take them for the same, and understand <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> with the rest of the <ns0:hi>Patriarches,</ns0:hi> to be both <ns0:hi>the first-Fruit,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Root.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> holy, the lump <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> also <ns0:hi>holy</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">By <ns0:hi>Lump</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Branches,</ns0:hi> he meanes, the people of the <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi> that descended of these holy <ns0:hi>Patriarkes,</ns0:hi> and sprung from them, as <ns0:hi>branches</ns0:hi> from a <ns0:hi>Root.</ns0:hi> The great Question is<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> In what sence they are said to be <ns0:hi>Holy?</ns0:hi> Or of what <ns0:hi>holiness</ns0:hi> doth he speak? It is not meant of inherent, but of federal, or Covenant <ns0:hi>Holiness</ns0:hi>; all in an outward and visible Covenant with God, were called <ns0:hi>Holy. vid. Exod.</ns0:hi> 19.6. <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 8.24. many common things are called <ns0:hi>Holy</ns0:hi> in Scrip<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ure, because Dedicated to God, and to his Service; yea, <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> though a place of great wickedness, is called a Holy City, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 27.53. In such a sence as this, the <ns0:hi>Iewes</ns0:hi> are still a holy People; They have an Hereditary kind of Dedication to God; they have a federal <ns0:hi>Holiness,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>relation</ns0:hi> to God, as be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing for ever Separated to him, in the <ns0:hi>Loynes</ns0:hi> of their <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> genitors; this can never be wholly forfeited, as be<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>g Granted to all the Posterity of the Holy <ns0:hi>Patriarkes:</ns0:hi> Therefore they are called <ns0:hi>The children of the covenant, which God made with their Fathers,</ns0:hi> Act. 2.39. <ns0:hi>vid.</ns0:hi> Act. 3.25. So then God will remember in his own Time, His Cove<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nant with the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> the Posterity of <ns0:hi>Abraham,</ns0:hi> &c. who are <ns0:hi>Beloved for their Fathers sake,</ns0:hi> ver. 28. Therefore, in the mean time, they should not look on themselves with Desperation; nor should the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> look on them with Disdain; as it follows in the next words.</ns0:note>: and if the root <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> holy, so <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> the branches.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17. <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>but if.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> And <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">In this, and some following Verses, the Apostle di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gresseth a little, and takes occasion to prevent the Insul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ting of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> over the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>; as also to perswade them to take Warning by their Example.</ns0:note> if <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jer. 11.16.</ns0:note> some of the branches be broken off <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>unbelie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving Iews.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and thou <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">A <ns0:hi>believing Gentile:</ns0:hi> Though he speaks as to a particular Person, yet he means the whole Body of the <ns0:hi>believing Gentiles.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> being a <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>a wild <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>live branch.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> wild olive tree <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">A <ns0:hi>Cion</ns0:hi> taken from <ns0:hi>a wild Olive tree. i. e.</ns0:hi> From the heathenish and unbelieving World.</ns0:note>, were graffed in <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>for them.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> amongst them <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>believing Iews.</ns0:hi> Some Read for them, or in the place of the <ns0:hi>branches,</ns0:hi> that are <ns0:hi>broken off.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">By the <ns0:hi>Root</ns0:hi> he means <ns0:hi>Abraham,</ns0:hi> &c. as before: By the <ns0:hi>Olive tree,</ns0:hi> he means the <ns0:hi>Church of Christ</ns0:hi>; by the <ns0:hi>Root,</ns0:hi> or Sap of the <ns0:hi>Root,</ns0:hi> and by the <ns0:hi>Fatness of the Olive tree,</ns0:hi> he means, All the Promises and Priviledges, the Graces and Ordinances, the spiritual Blessings and Benefits, which belonged to <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi> and his <ns0:hi>Seed,</ns0:hi> or to the <ns0:hi>true Church of God.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18. Boast not against the branches: <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Against the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> who, because of their <ns0:hi>unbe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lief,</ns0:hi> are <ns0:hi>broken off</ns0:hi>; as if by Nature thou wert better than they, or more worthy of that Grace which is bestowed on thee. The word signifies, Throw not up thy Neck, don't carry thy self Scornfully and Insultingly.</ns0:note> But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> If any will needs be so Insolent, let them know and consider, That as the <ns0:hi>Root</ns0:hi> is not beholding to the <ns0:hi>branches,</ns0:hi> but the <ns0:hi>branches</ns0:hi> to the <ns0:hi>Root:</ns0:hi> So the good Things that the <ns0:hi>Gen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiles</ns0:hi> have, they receiv'd from the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> and not the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> from them: The <ns0:hi>Gentile</ns0:hi> Church is Incorporated into the <ns0:hi>Iewish,</ns0:hi> and not the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> into the <ns0:hi>Gentile.</ns0:hi> Or else the meaning is, Despise not the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> for they are the natu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral <ns0:hi>branches</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Root</ns0:hi> that <ns0:hi>bears them. If thou Insultest</ns0:hi> over the <ns0:hi>Branches,</ns0:hi> thou dost in a manner lift up thy self against the <ns0:hi>Root:</ns0:hi> That once <ns0:hi>bore</ns0:hi> them, and now <ns0:hi>bears</ns0:hi> thee; even <ns0:hi>Abraham,</ns0:hi> who is the Father of all them that <ns0:hi>Believe. Abraham</ns0:hi> is not the <ns0:hi>Root,</ns0:hi> simply and absolutely, but Relatively, or by way of Relation to his Posterity and Off-spring.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be graffed in.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20. Well; because of unbelief they were bro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken off <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Here he brings in the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> alleadging a Reason for their Insulting over the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>; because the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were <ns0:hi>broken off,</ns0:hi> that they might give place, or make way for them; and the <ns0:hi>less worthy,</ns0:hi> do alwayes give place to the <ns0:hi>more worthy.</ns0:hi> To this he Answers, <ns0:hi>First</ns0:hi> by way of Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cession: Well <ns0:hi>(saith he)</ns0:hi> it is true, and I do not deny it, That the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were <ns0:hi>broken off,</ns0:hi> that the <ns0:hi>Gentiles might be graffed in:</ns0:hi> But then he further adds, by way of Correcti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on or Negation; That the Worthiness of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> was not the cause why the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> were <ns0:hi>broken off</ns0:hi>; but it was because of their own Unbelief; they would not Accept of Christ, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.11. They went <ns0:hi>about to establish their own righteousness,</ns0:hi> and would <ns0:hi>not submit themselves to the Righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ousness of God,</ns0:hi> as 'tis in <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 10.3. Therefore, if you <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> shall Reason after this manner, you plainly put a Fallacy upon your selves, and take that for a Cause which is none: You don't distinguish between the <ns0:hi>cause</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>event</ns0:hi>; it fell out indeed, That the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> being cast off, the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> were received in, but this was not the Cause of that.</ns0:note>, and thou <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> standest by faith <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> Neither is thy Worthiness the Cause of thy present Standing in the room of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>; or of ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving thy Station in the Church of Christ; but it is thy <ns0:hi>believing</ns0:hi> in that <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> whom the <ns0:hi>Iews rejected.</ns0:hi> By <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> thou wast first <ns0:hi>Engraffed,</ns0:hi> and still continuest in the good <ns0:hi>Olive-tree.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>. Be not high-minded, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Prov. 28.14. Isa. 66.2. Phil. 2.12.</ns0:note> but fear <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> Be advised, and take heed of be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing Self-conceited and Secure; if thou fall into their Fault, thou mayest expect the same Fate. Therefore stand in Awe, and Sin not: Thou art subject to Unbelief and Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stasy, as well as they.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21. For if God spared not the natural b<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ches, <ns0:hi>take heed</ns0:hi> lest he also spare not thee <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">This Verse is a Reason of the forementioned Admo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nition. <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> If God proceeded with so much Severity a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst his Ancient People the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> you <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> may in Reason expect as great Severity, if you take not heed to your selves, and to your Standing.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22. Behold therefore the goodness, and seve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rity of God: on them which fell, severity; but towards thee, goodness, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 15.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Heb. 3.6, 14.</ns0:note> if thou continue in <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> goodness: Otherwise <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Job. 15.2.</ns0:note> thou also shalt be cut off <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">In this Verse, he farther perswades the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> to Humility, and Godly Fear; and suggesteth several Reasons for it. The <ns0:hi>First</ns0:hi> is taken from the Example of God's <ns0:hi>se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verity</ns0:hi> to the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> they falling into Apostacy and Unbe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lief; are generally <ns0:hi>cut off</ns0:hi> and cast away. A <ns0:hi>Second</ns0:hi> Rea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />son is taken from the <ns0:hi>free-grace,</ns0:hi> and undeserved <ns0:hi>goodness of God</ns0:hi> to the poor <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> who were mercifully Planted or <ns0:hi>Graffed</ns0:hi> in the room of the <ns0:hi>Iews.</ns0:hi> A <ns0:hi>Third</ns0:hi> Reason is taken from the Condition of their present Standing, which is, if they continue in His Goodness. <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> If they continue in that State wherein His Goodness hath set them. Some think, the Cause is here put for the Effect; the <ns0:hi>goodness of God</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>faith,</ns0:hi> which was wrought in them by the <ns0:hi>good<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>grace of God.</ns0:hi> The Antithesis, in th<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> next Verse, shews this to be the Sence, For there he speaks of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> not continuing, or abiding still in Unbelief. A <ns0:hi>Fourth</ns0:hi> Reason is from the Danger that would follow, If through <ns0:hi>pride</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>security</ns0:hi> they should Fall and Miscarry, they would be <ns0:hi>cut off</ns0:hi> as the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>natural Branches</ns0:hi> are. Some observe the change of the Word, The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> are said to be <ns0:hi>broken off,</ns0:hi> but the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> would be <ns0:hi>cut off</ns0:hi>; they would as it were be stock't up by the <ns0:hi>Roots</ns0:hi>; but that seems too critical and curious.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23. And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be graffed in: For God is able <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Cor. 3<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> to graff them in again <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Here he Adds another Argument, to repress the Ar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rogance, and Insulting of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi>; and 'tis taken from the Hope of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> Restauration. Though for the pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sent, they seem to be in a desperate, and forlorn Condi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion; yet the Restoring, and Re-engraffing of them into the Church, is not impossible. The great Obstacle is their Unbelief, which God is able to remove. The same God that <ns0:hi>rejected</ns0:hi> them, is able to <ns0:hi>restore</ns0:hi> them: To Him all Things are possible, He can cause dead and dry <ns0:hi>Bones</ns0:hi> to Live. An Argument from the Power of God (and that in the very words of this Text) is frequently made use of in Scripture, to excite <ns0:hi>hope</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>assurance, Chap.</ns0:hi> 4.21. and 14.4. 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 9.8. 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.12. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 2.18. and 11.19.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:426" />24. For if thou wert <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> off <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> the Olive <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>, which is <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> to thee.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> cut out of the olive-tree which is wild by nature, and wert graffed contrary to nature into a good olive-tree; how much more shall these which be the <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>these <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> are <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> to <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tural <ns0:hi>branches,</ns0:hi> be graffed into their own olive-tree <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">He here shews the Probability, as well as Possibility of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> Conversion; because God hath done that which is more unlikely. <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> If the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> which were a kind of <ns0:hi>wild Olive branches,</ns0:hi> were <ns0:hi>graffed into a good Olive tree,</ns0:hi> the Church of God, which is contrary to Nature, seeing Men use to <ns0:hi>graff</ns0:hi> a good <ns0:hi>Cion</ns0:hi> into a <ns0:hi>wild</ns0:hi> stock (as an Ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple into a Crab) and not a <ns0:hi>wild Cion</ns0:hi> into a good Stock; how much more shall the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> which are the <ns0:hi>natural branches</ns0:hi>; yea, <ns0:hi>branches</ns0:hi> of that <ns0:hi>Olive-tree,</ns0:hi> into which the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> are now <ns0:hi>Engraffed</ns0:hi>; be <ns0:hi>graffed</ns0:hi> into their own <ns0:hi>O<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />live-tree,</ns0:hi> to which formerly they did belong: According to the Custom of <ns0:hi>graffing,</ns0:hi> which was common amongst them, to <ns0:hi>graff</ns0:hi> one <ns0:hi>tree</ns0:hi> upon another, of the same kind; and grounded on <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 19.19.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25. For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery lest ye should be wise in your own conceits that <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> blindness in part is hapned to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Here he shews there is, not only a Possibility and Probability, but a Certainty of the <ns0:hi>Iews conversion</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>calling.</ns0:hi> This he calleth a <ns0:hi>Mystery,</ns0:hi> or a Secret; though it was <ns0:hi>revealed</ns0:hi> in the <ns0:hi>Scripture</ns0:hi> (as you will hear) yet it was not understood; nay, the Manner, the Number, and the time of their <ns0:hi>Conversion,</ns0:hi> is still concealed and hid from us. The <ns0:hi>calling</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> was a <ns0:hi>Mystery,</ns0:hi> and a great <ns0:hi>Secret, vid. Ephes.</ns0:hi> 3.3. And so is the <ns0:hi>calling</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>restau<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ration</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Iews.</ns0:hi> There are <ns0:hi>Three</ns0:hi> Particulars of this <ns0:hi>Mystery,</ns0:hi> which he makes known to the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> (and he doth it the rather, lest they should swell with a high Conceit of themselves, and proudly despise the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>): Two of them are in this Verse; And the <ns0:hi>First</ns0:hi> is, That <ns0:hi>blindness</ns0:hi> is hapned to <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> in part only, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> They were not all Blinded or Hardned; or this <ns0:hi>blindness</ns0:hi> should not last alwayes, but for a time. The latter Sence agrees best with the word <ns0:hi>Mystery</ns0:hi>; for it was no <ns0:hi>secret,</ns0:hi> that some of the <ns0:hi>Iews believed</ns0:hi>; this was told them before, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 2, 5, 7. <ns0:hi>Secondly,</ns0:hi> Another part of this <ns0:hi>Mystery</ns0:hi> was, That this <ns0:hi>blindness</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> should continue till the <ns0:hi>Fulness of the Gentiles came in.</ns0:hi> By <ns0:hi>Fulness</ns0:hi> here, (as in <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 12.) understand a great Number or Multitude of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi>; greater, by far, than was in the <ns0:hi>Apostles</ns0:hi> days. There is another Exposition of this Clause, which I sub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mit to Consideration: By the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> here you may un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstand the <ns0:hi>Romans,</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>Roman Monarchy</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Power (vid. Act.</ns0:hi> 4.27. and 21.11.) And by the <ns0:hi>coming in</ns0:hi> of their <ns0:hi>Fulness,</ns0:hi> may be understood, the <ns0:hi>full time</ns0:hi> of their Reign and Continuance; after which their Ruine follows. And so here is foretold the time of the <ns0:hi>calling</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> which will be soon after the Destruction of <ns0:hi>Antichrist,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Roman</ns0:hi> Hierarchy. <ns0:hi>Query,</ns0:hi> Whether this doth not agree with the <ns0:hi>Prediction</ns0:hi> of our <ns0:hi>Saviour?</ns0:hi> Luk. 21.24.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26. And so all Israel shall be saved <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Here is a <ns0:hi>Third</ns0:hi> and chief <ns0:hi>part</ns0:hi> of the afore-mentioned <ns0:hi>Mystery,</ns0:hi> that in the end, All <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> shall be Saved. By <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> is not meant the whole Church of God, consisting of <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi>; so that word is used, <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 6.16. <ns0:hi>& alibi.</ns0:hi> For then, what he spake would have been no <ns0:hi>Mystery</ns0:hi> at all; but by <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> here (as in the precedent Verse) you must understand, the Nation and People of the <ns0:hi>Iews.</ns0:hi> And by all <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> is not meant every individual <ns0:hi>Israelite,</ns0:hi> but many, or (it may be) the greatest part of them. So all is to be taken in Scripture, <ns0:hi>vid. Iohn</ns0:hi> 6.45. 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2.6. <ns0:hi>& alibi.</ns0:hi> Look as when he speaks of the Conversion of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>coming in</ns0:hi> of their <ns0:hi>fulness,</ns0:hi> there are many (too many of them) still Uncon<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verted. So notwithstanding the general <ns0:hi>calling</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> a great many of them may remain uncalled.</ns0:note>: as it is written <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The Apostle had this by Revelation, but he proves it also by Scripture. All are not agreed, from whence these Testi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />monies are taken; the Former is found (with some little variation, in <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 59.20. As for the Latter, some think it is taken from <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 31.33. Others think, that he joyn<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth two places in <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> together (as he did before, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 8.) and the last words are taken out of <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 27.9. The <ns0:hi>Se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venty</ns0:hi> have the very words used by the <ns0:hi>Apostle.</ns0:hi> These <ns0:hi>Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phesies</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Promises,</ns0:hi> though they were in part <ns0:hi>fulfilled,</ns0:hi> when Christ came in the Flesh (<ns0:hi>vid. Act.</ns0:hi> 3.26.) yet there will be a more full and conpleat Accomplishment thereof, upon the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Nation and People, towards the end of the World.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">

                     </ns0:gap>. 14.7. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">

                     </ns0:gap> 16.</ns0:note> There shall come out of Sion the deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27. For this <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28. As concerning the Gospel, <ns0:hi>they are</ns0:hi> ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies for your sake; but as touching the electi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on, <ns0:hi>they are</ns0:hi> beloved for the fathers sakes <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Here an Objection is obviated; the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> might Object and say, The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> can never return and be Saved; forasmuch as they have <ns0:hi>rejected</ns0:hi> the Gospel, and are there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore hated of God. To this he Answers by way of Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cession, that it was true indeed, They had <ns0:hi>rejected</ns0:hi> the Gos<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pel, and for this they were <ns0:hi>rejected</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>hated</ns0:hi> of God; but this hapned well to the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> and was to their Ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vantage; for the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> refusal of the Gospel, brought it sooner to them (<ns0:hi>vid. ver.</ns0:hi> 11.) Or else the meaning is, They are Enemies of God, and of his Gospel; and the ra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther <ns0:hi>reject</ns0:hi> it, because you <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> embrace it: They think the worse of the Gospel, because you <ns0:hi>believe</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>profess</ns0:hi> it. Then he adds by way of Correction, That they were not yet in such desperate Circumstances; but in regard of <ns0:hi>Election, they are beloved for the Fathers sakes.</ns0:hi> By <ns0:hi>Election,</ns0:hi> he means, Either God's Choosing them to eternal Life: Or rather, His Choosing that Nation and People, above all other Nations and People of the World, to be his peculiar People. <ns0:hi>vid. Deut.</ns0:hi> 7.6. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 135.4. <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 13.46. And by God's Love to them, he means, His Love of <ns0:hi>good Will,</ns0:hi> which He had to that People still, <ns0:hi>for their Fathers sakes:</ns0:hi> Not because of the Merit of their <ns0:hi>Fathers,</ns0:hi> but be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause of the Covenant made with their <ns0:hi>Fathers</ns0:hi>; because they are Descended of those <ns0:hi>Fathers,</ns0:hi> to whom God had Promised, That He would be their God, and the God of their <ns0:hi>Seed</ns0:hi> after them; Aye, and of their <ns0:hi>Seeds Seed</ns0:hi> for ever; which Promises of God, the infidelity of many of them, can't wholly frustrate.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29. For the gifts and calling of God <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Num. 23.19.</ns0:note> without repentance <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">These words considered simply, and abstractedly, afford this Truth; That the special Gifts of God, his Election, Justification, Adoption, and in particular effectual <ns0:hi>Calling,</ns0:hi> are irrevocable. God never repents of giving, nor we of receiving them. 'Tis otherwise with common Gifts and Graces, 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 15.11. But if you consider these words Relatively, as you respect what went before; the Sence seems to be this, That the <ns0:hi>gifts and calling of God,</ns0:hi> where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />by He was pleas'd to Adopt the Posterity of <ns0:hi>Abraham</ns0:hi>; and to engage Himself by Covenant to them, are invio<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lable, and are such as shall never be reversed or repented of.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30. For as ye in times past <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>formerly were disobedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ent.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> have not be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieved God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31. Even so have these also now <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>not o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />beyed.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> not be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieved, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">This is the last Argument, to prove the <ns0:hi>conversion</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>calling</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> which is further confirm'd, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 32. The Argument is taken from the like dealing of God with the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> after a long time of infidelity, he received them to Mercy; therefore He will also at last Receive the <ns0:hi>Iews.</ns0:hi> He Argues from the Less to the Greater; If the infidelity of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> was the occasion of <ns0:hi>mercy</ns0:hi> to the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> much more shall the <ns0:hi>mercy</ns0:hi> shewed to the <ns0:hi>Gen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tiles,</ns0:hi> be an occasion of shewing Mercy to the <ns0:hi>Iews. q. d.</ns0:hi> There is more Force in that which is good, to pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />duce a good Effect, than in that which is evil, to have a good Event: Therefore, if the <ns0:hi>Vnbelief</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had so good an Event, as to occasion the Conversion of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi>; Why may we not think, That the <ns0:hi>calling</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> will contribute to the Conversion of the <ns0:hi>Iews? (vid. ver.</ns0:hi> 11, 14.) when the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> shall see the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> Mercy, <ns0:hi>i. e. God</ns0:hi>'s <ns0:hi>Mercy</ns0:hi> to them: How the whole World flourisheth under the Profession of Christianity; how the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> is in vain expected by them; how their Nation is dispersed, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> Then they shall at last come in and cleave to <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> and be mercifully Received by Him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32. For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 3.9.</ns0:note> God hath <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>shut up all together.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> God hath, in just Judgment, shut up both <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gettiles,</ns0:hi> equally and successively, in <ns0:hi>unbelief,</ns0:hi> as in a Prison, that so, in His own time, He might fulfill the Coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sel of his <ns0:hi>Will,</ns0:hi> in shewing undeserved <ns0:hi>mercy unto all; i. e.</ns0:hi> Unto both <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi>; First the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> and then the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi>; and then at last, both to <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gentiles.</ns0:hi> By <ns0:hi>All</ns0:hi> here, the means, Those that shall <ns0:hi>believe,</ns0:hi> whether of one sort or of the other, as appears from that parallel place, <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 3.22. <ns0:hi>Luther,</ns0:hi> in a very great Conflict, had much Support from this Text.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:427" />33. <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">In this, and the following Verses, is the Conclusion of all that he had delivered; especially in this, and the Two preceding Chapters. He had spoken of many pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />found <ns0:hi>Mysteries</ns0:hi>; and Answered many critical Questions: And here he makes a Pause, and falls into an Admiration of God, his abundant <ns0:hi>Wisdom</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Knowledge.</ns0:hi> He seems here to be like a Man that wades into the Waters, till he begins to feel no Bottom, and then he cryes out, <ns0:hi>O the depth!</ns0:hi> and goes no farther.</ns0:note> O <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 36.6.</ns0:note> the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> The unmeasurable, unconceivable Abundance of his <ns0:hi>Wisdom</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Knowledge.</ns0:hi> Some distinguish these, Two; Others take them for the same, <ns0:hi>vid. Col.</ns0:hi> 2.3.</ns0:note>! <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Job 11.7.</ns0:note> how un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />searchable <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> his judgments, and his ways <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>not to be traced.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> past finding out <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Some distinguish betwixt the <ns0:hi>Iudg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ments</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>wayes of God</ns0:hi>; By the Former, Understanding his Decrees and Purposes concerning <ns0:hi>Nations</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Persons:</ns0:hi> By the Latter, The Methods of his Providence in his Deal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ings with them: Others think the same thing is meant by an Ingemination, which is Familiar amongst the <ns0:hi>Hebrews.</ns0:hi> He sayes, of <ns0:hi>God</ns0:hi>'s <ns0:hi>Iudgments,</ns0:hi> That they are <ns0:hi>unsearchable</ns0:hi>; therefore, not to be Complained of, Censured, or to be narrowly Pryed into; and of <ns0:hi>his wayes,</ns0:hi> that they are past finding out; the same in Sence with <ns0:hi>unsearchable:</ns0:hi> 'Tis a Metaphor from Hounds, who have no Footstep or Scent of the Game which they pursue: Nor can Men trace the <ns0:hi>Lord,</ns0:hi> or find out the Reason of his Doings; as none can Line out the Way of a Ship in the Sea, or an Eagle in the Air, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> Some restrain the Sence, to the <ns0:hi>wayes of God</ns0:hi> in disposing and ordering the <ns0:hi>Election</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Rejection</ns0:hi> of Men.</ns0:note>!</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34. For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jer. 23.18. 1 Cor. 2.16.</ns0:note> who hath known the mind of the Lord, or <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Job 36.22.</ns0:note> who hath been his counsel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lor <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e. Who</ns0:hi> knoweth what God is about to do, or <ns0:hi>who</ns0:hi> hath given his Advice about the Doing of it? This is ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken out of <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 40.13, 14.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35. Or who hath first given to him, and it shall be recompensed to him again <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>q. d.</ns0:hi> If any Man hath obliged God, by any thing he hath done for Him, he shall have an ample Reward. Al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />luding (as some think) to <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 41.11. But seeing this can<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />not be, and that God is Indebted unto none; therefore the Salvation of <ns0:hi>all,</ns0:hi> is of meer <ns0:hi>grace</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>mercy</ns0:hi>; and there is no cause of Complaining, if He deal more Bountifully with some, than with others.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36. For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor 8.6. Col. 1.16.</ns0:note> of him, and through him, and to him <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> all things <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>i. e. All things</ns0:hi> are of <ns0:hi>him,</ns0:hi> as the efficient Cause; <ns0:hi>through him,</ns0:hi> as the disposing Cause; to <ns0:hi>Him</ns0:hi> as the final Cause. They are of <ns0:hi>Him,</ns0:hi> without any other Motive; <ns0:hi>through him,</ns0:hi> without any assistance; and <ns0:hi>to him,</ns0:hi> without any other end, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> For his Sake alone.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:hi>to him.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> To whom <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> glory for ever. Amen <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">An usual Doxology in Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ture, <ns0:hi>vid. Gal.</ns0:hi> 1.5. 2 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 4.18. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 13.21. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 5.11.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
